version.changelog: Comprehensive OpenClaw operations skill combining CLI mastery, gateway admin, security hardening, troubleshooting playbooks, channel management, agent orchestration, and production best practices

llm.summary: The skill appears to be an operations playbook for OpenClaw and contains plausible, sensitive operational commands, but its metadata is incomplete (no declared required binary or config paths and no source/homepage), which is inconsistent with its claimed CLI-heavy purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name and description claim broad OpenClaw operational capabilities (gateway, channels, secrets, tokens, repair), which matches the SKILL.md content. However, the registry metadata declares no required binaries or config paths even though the instructions rely heavily on an 'openclaw' CLI and reference local config files (openclaw.json, credentials/, sessions/). The missing declaration of the CLI is an incoherence worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run many sensitive commands (security audit --fix, doctor --repair --non-interactive, generate-gateway-token, secrets get/set/delete, sessions kill, channels repair, network discovery --wide). This is within scope for an ops skill, but the instructions allow potentially destructive or exfiltrative actions and include non-interactive repair modes. The document mentions safety practices (backup, verify) but does not enforce or require confirmation; that leaves room for accidental destructive actions if an agent runs commands autonomously.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present; SKILL.md is instruction-only. That minimizes install-time risk because nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials in metadata, which superficially limits its privileges. However, the instructions manipulate secrets and generate gateway tokens and reference local credential directories — operations that typically require elevated access or confirmation. The metadata also does not declare required config paths or the need for the openclaw CLI binary, making the declared environment access inconsistent with the operational actions described.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system-wide settings. Model invocation is allowed (default), which means an agent could invoke it autonomously; this is the platform default and not by itself a red flag. There is no instruction in SKILL.md to modify other skills or agent-wide configurations beyond standard OpenClaw operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an operations runbook that instructs running many sensitive OpenClaw CLI commands (including generating tokens, modifying secrets, and non-interactive repair). That can be legitimate for an ops helper, but note: (1) the package metadata omits declaring the 'openclaw' CLI and config paths it clearly needs — a sign of sloppy or incomplete packaging; (2) the SKILL.md permits destructive/non-interactive fixes and token generation, so running it without oversight could change system state or expose secrets. Before installing: verify the skill's source or prefer a skill with a published homepage/repo, ensure you have tested backups (openclaw.json, credentials/, sessions/), run commands in dry-run or interactive mode where available, restrict autonomous invocation if you don't want automatic repairs, and consider running the skill in an isolated/test environment until you confirm behavior. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for missing metadata (required binaries, config paths) and a repo/homepage before proceeding.
